title: Adams v. Northeast Presbytery
disposition_detail: SJC found the complaint administratively out of order on two grounds: (1) BCO 43-1 barred a complaint about a matter that was the subject of an appeal in another case; and (2) the complaint requested the accused be retried on matters of which his presbytery had acquitted him, relief not within the SJC's power. The related appeal was later withdrawn and the withdrawal approved, but the SJC still ruled the complaint out of order on BCO 43-1. No merits ruling was made.
first_summary: Adams complained after Northeast Presbytery ruled his complaint out of order in a judicial case. The SJC dismissed the complaint as out of order because BCO 43-1 barred a complaint about a matter then on appeal, and because Adams sought retrial on acquitted charges. The related appeal was later withdrawn, but the SJC still treated the complaint as barred. A concurrence disagreed with the first ground and discussed appellate review of acquittals.
summary: A prosecutor's complaint relating to Northeast Presbytery's judicial case was held administratively out of order by the SJC. The SJC adopted two grounds: BCO 43-1 bars a complaint about a matter subject to an appeal in another case, and the complaint sought retrial of an accused on charges of which he had been acquitted, relief the SJC could not grant. Although the related appeal was later withdrawn and the withdrawal approved, the SJC still applied BCO 43-1. A concurrence disputed that first ground and urged BCO clarification of appellate review of acquittals. No merits ruling was made.

evidence_notes.dispute: Prosecutor Adams filed a complaint after a Northeast Presbytery judicial commission found a minister guilty on 3 of 12 charges and Presbytery approved the judgment; the minister appealed (Case 99-3), and Presbytery ruled Adams's complaint out of order under BCO 43-1 (lines 35-37).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: SJC found the complaint administratively out of order on two grounds: BCO 43-1 because it concerned a matter subject to an appeal in another case, and because Adams sought retrial on matters of which the accused had been acquitted, relief outside SJC power (lines 17, 31, 39, 43-49).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The related appeal was later withdrawn and the withdrawal approved, yet the SJC still considered the complaint out of order on BCO 43-1 (line 37). The concurrence agreed with the judgment but disputed the first ground and urged BCO clarification on appellate review of acquittals (lines 31, 39, 51-73); no merits ruling on acquittal review was adopted.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Case 99-3 is referenced only as an appeal that was withdrawn and approved; no incorporated decision text is supplied. Lower court and presbytery actions are procedural history, not adopted reasons (lines 35-37).

source_limits: Official report excerpt only; it does not include the full complaint, the lower court record, or the text of Case 99-3. The only supplied separate opinion is Donahoe's concurrence; Miller's partial dissent appears only in the roll call. No merits review of the acquittal issue is supplied.
